  • Alabama↗Texas community/government connection

    Texas community/government connection

    Tribe's account identifies the joint Alabama-Coushatta community's reservation in southeast Texas. Not a government for every Alabama person.

  • Caddo↗Historical homeland connection
    Connection & source
    Historical homeland connection

    Actual NPS history/map caption explicitly identifies East Texas Caddo communities in 1687; historical geography only.

    Historical Caddo communities, including 1687 map-caption geography. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Coahuiltecan↗Historical regional umbrella in specialist reference
    Connection & source
    Historical regional umbrella in specialist reference

    Actual introductory and geographic sections place this broad historical label in southern Texas and northeastern Mexico. The article emphasizes many autonomous named groups and uncertain classification. This route does not assert one unified people/government, adopt extinction claims or establish modern recognition.

    Historical geography described in Handbook of Texas; inspected 2026-10-21. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Coushatta↗Texas community/government connection

    Texas community/government connection

    Tribe's account distinguishes Coushatta leaders within the joint Texas community. This specific government does not represent every Coushatta community.

    Historical and continuing Texas setting. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

  • Jumano↗Historical community region connection
    Connection & source
    Historical community region connection

    Actual Texas House resolution identifies Jumano history in West Texas. Commemorative legislative source, not federal or state recognition instrument; no descent totals imported.

    Sixteenth–nineteenth-century geography; 2019 resolution. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗
  • Karankawa↗Traditional coastal homeland in specialist scholarship
    Connection & source
    Traditional coastal homeland in specialist scholarship

    The essay explicitly locates traditional Karankawa homelands on Texas's Gulf Coast and explains that the name encompasses several coastal groups. Only the broad Texas connection is indexed; the account does not justify collapsing the groups into a single historical government.

    Traditional and early-contact homeland described in the revised reference essay. Reviewed 2026-10-21.

    Read the supporting source ↗

These are starting lists, not a complete census. Modern borders help you navigate; they are not Indigenous homeland boundaries. A connection may be historical or present-day and does not imply presence throughout a region. Directory names can overlap; the profiles explain their relationships.
